title: Field Pitch Playbook: Platform Value, Pricing Tiers, and Security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook equips field reps and solutions engineers with a concise, repeatable pitch for Redwood Inference that ties developer-focused product positioning to concrete pricing examples and a short security FAQ for prospect conversations. Use the one-pager for discovery calls, expand into the pitch deck for executive meetings, and hand off pricing anchors to commercial for proposal generation.

Use cases targeted by this playbook
- Product teams adding chat, summarization, or semantic search to existing SaaS products.
- Platform/infra teams standardizing inference across multiple product lines.
- Regulated customers requiring private deployments and auditability.

Core positioning (elevator)
- Redwood Inference: the developer-first runtime that makes LLM inference predictable, low-cost, and reliable from prototype to scale.
- Key value props: predictable performance across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; actionable cost controls (batching, caching, quantization); and enterprise-grade observability and fallbacks to maintain uptime.

Persona messaging (snippets for slides or email)
- Platform Engineer: "Stop wasting cycles redesigning model serving. Redwood gives you a single API and routing policies so teams can deploy consistent inference across cloud/private with SLOs you can measure."
- ML Engineer: "Reduce per-token cost without retraining: quantization profiles, KV caching, and model variants give predictable latency and 20–60% reduction in serving spend for common workloads."
- Product Manager: "Ship features faster: same API for hosted and private, built-in rollouts, and tracing hooks for quality regressions."

Competitive brief (one-paragraph summary + comparison)
- Short take: Redwood emphasizes production economics — predictable latency, transparent unit cost controls, and a unified developer experience across deployment modes. Against generic cloud AI endpoints, Redwood offers more production tooling and dedicated capacity options. Against self-hosted runtimes, Redwood offers faster time-to-value plus optional private deployments that preserve enterprise controls.

Quick comparison (for call notes — read aloud rather than send verbatim)
- Competitor: Generic Cloud AI Provider	| Strengths: Model catalog, scale	| Gaps vs Redwood: fewer deployment modes, limited dedicated capacity options.
- Competitor: Self-hosted Runtime Vendor	| Strengths: Full control on-prem	| Gaps vs Redwood: Upfront ops burden, less integrated monitoring & rollout tooling.
- Competitor: Vertical AI Specialist	| Strengths: Domain-tuned models	| Gaps vs Redwood: Lock-in, less flexible routing and cost tooling.

Sales play and discovery checklist (use in first meeting)
1) Ask about current inference spend and billing cadence (monthly, committed, forecasted).
2) Identify peak qps and 95th percentile latency targets for typical request sizes.
3) Confirm data residency / compliance constraints and if a private deployment is required.
4) Learn who owns deployment (platform infra, ML infra, or product engineering).
5) Evaluate tolerance for model quality regressions and existing eval/monitoring practices.

Pricing guidance (anchor examples and negotiation levers)
- Principles: Start with consumption transparency; show per-unit math; offer committed reserved capacity for predictable load. Always convert token rates to $/MAU or $/feature-call for the customer's unit economics.

Anchors (examples for initial conversations)
- Hosted Starter (self-serve): $0.05 per 1k prompt tokens, $0.10 per 1k completion tokens, embeddings $0.001 per vector. Monthly volume up to 10M tokens; basic SLAs and console access.
- Dedicated Basic (reserved capacity): starting at $8,000/month for a 2x A100-equivalent pool with predictable throughput (up to 400k tokens/min sustained), 99.9% monthly uptime SLA, and 30-day billing. Includes autoscaling policy and cost breakdown reports.
- Dedicated Enterprise: custom reserved pools, enterprise SLAs (99.95% uptime), burst capacity, priority support, and access to advanced quantization profiles and model variant management. Typical entry: $25k+/month.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) Licensing: platform fee + deployment cost. Example anchor: $120k/year platform license + professional services (typical 6–12 week deployment). Add-ons: audit log retention, HSM integration.

Negotiation levers for sales engineers
- Increase commitment term (12→24 months) for deeper discounts.
- Swap token-based billing for a blended reserved rate for customers with stable throughput.
- Offer a short pilot discount (6–8 weeks) tied to a POC success metric: e.g., 40% cost reduction vs baseline or P95 latency < target.
- Bundle observability retention or advanced SLAs as paid add-ons.

How to present pricing in a proposal (recommended structure)
1) Executive summary: business outcome and recommended package.
2) Pricing table: line items with units (tokens, reserved capacity, add-ons).
3) Assumptions: sequence lengths, qps profiles, model variants.
4) Success criteria and pilot length.
5) Next steps and implementation timeline (owner names and estimated dates).

Pitch deck outline (6–8 slides, fast executive meeting)
- Slide 1: Title + quick value statement (1 sentence).
- Slide 2: Problem: cost, latency, and fragmentation of inference stacks.
- Slide 3: Redwood solution: unified API, routing, and dev-first tooling.
- Slide 4: Live metrics / benchmark: typical 95th latency and cost delta vs cloud-hosted baseline.
- Slide 5: Deployment options & security controls (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Slide 6: Pricing and recommended engagement (pilot → reserved).
- Slide 7: Case study summary + success metrics.
- Slide 8: Next steps and legal/compliance checklist.

Field-ready objection responses (short)
- "We already have a model infra team": Agree + ask how much of their cycles are spent on infra vs product. Offer pilot scope to offload common patterns (routing, caching, rollouts).
- "Cheaper to self-host": Acknowledge fixed-cost tradeoffs; show time-to-market and operational cost reductions, and offer a blended reserved pricing example.
- "We need on-prem due to compliance": Walk through Private deployment timeline (4–12 weeks typical) and highlight KMS/HSM and audit log integration.

Case study (one-paragraph proof)
- Customer: BrightWrite (midmarket SaaS, content generation at scale)
- Engagement: 8-week pilot → Dedicated Basic
- Outcome: Reduced per-generation cost by 42% through batching, KV caching, and a quantization profile; 3x improvement in 95th-percentile latency for 512-token completions; SLA-backed uptime met across a seasonal usage spike. Result: BrightWrite signed a 12-month reserved contract at a 30% uplift vs pilot monthly run-rate.

Operational handoff checklist (post-PO)
- Assign Redwood success owner and customer technical lead.
- Share traffic profile and auth requirements (API keys, IP allowlists).
- Agree on rollout policy: canary percentages, rollback thresholds, and eval prompts for quality checks.
- Schedule 2-week cadence for first 90 days: invoicing review, latency cost reports, and model quality monitoring.

Security & compliance FAQ (prospect-facing quick answers)
1) Q: How do you protect customer data in Hosted?
   A: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256). Access to production logs is role-limited; Redwood never uses customer data to train public models unless contractually agreed. Audit logs capture request/response metadata and are available for export.
2) Q: Can we run in our VPC / on-prem?
   A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC-integration and on-prem packaging. Typical VPC onboarding is 4–8 weeks; full on-prem deployments are 6–12 weeks depending on approvals and hardware procurement.
3) Q: Key management and HSM support?
   A: We integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and offer HSM-backed keys for private deployments.
4) Q: Do you provide SOC2 / ISO evidence?
   A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 artefacts (summary available under NDA). We also support custom audits in enterprise engagements.
5) Q: How is RBAC and least-privilege enforced?
   A: Token-level RBAC in the Console, per-route API keys, and SSO (OIDC/SAML) for Console access. Admin and billing roles are separate from deploy/usage roles.
6) Q: Can we get audit logging and long-term retention?
   A: Yes. Audit log retention is configurable; long-term retention is an add-on (30/90/365+ day options) and supports export to customer S3 or SIEM.
7) Q: What SLAs do you offer?
   A: Hosted: 99.9% availability for paid tiers; Dedicated Enterprise: 99.95% with financial credits. Latency SLAs are contractual for Dedicated pools (e.g., P95 < 200ms for 512-token workloads under specified load profiles).
8) Q: How do you handle vulnerability disclosure and incident response?
   A: We have a published security contact, triage timelines (initial acknowledgement within 24 hours), and incident response runbooks. We perform regular pentests and publish summary reports to customers under NDA.
